clue.text: Five diamonds the boy gives colonial dignitary

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
ice is slang for diamonds
Roy is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad hands over a five of diamonds to a dignitary of the colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A viceroy governed a colony or province on behalf of the monarch, a high colonial official.

clue.text: Point to a weapon a war horde deployed

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out and rearranged, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A horde of warriors is deployed, pointed at a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges the letters of A WAR HORDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tip of an arrow is the business end of that weapon.

clue.text: Calling up about something in the paper

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters built here are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an item is a piece in a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone phones up about a story in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run RE + ITEM, read upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is one's vocation or trade, the sense of the French-derived word for a profession.

clue.text: Fowl attacking ducks? Another bird!

parts.note: a cock is a male domestic fowl
to be at someone is to attack them
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so ducks are two Os

explanation.surface: A farmyard bird goes for some ducks, and then a parrot turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a batter's score of zero, so 'ducks' gives OO.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockatoo is a crested parrot, so it is a further species of bird beyond the fowl and ducks.

clue.text: Overheated hikers in bloomers

parts.note: someone overheated goes red in the face
ramblers are walkers in the countryside

explanation.surface: Walkers who have got too hot while wearing old-fashioned baggy knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like underwear but means flowers; the climbing rose of this name has deep red blooms. Rambling is the British word for country hiking.
explanation.definitionFit: This climbing rose is a flowering plant, and a bloomer is a crossword's playful word for something that flowers.

clue.text: One of the marooned actors on tour

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a show
a touring company is away from home

explanation.surface: A member of a touring company finds themselves stranded.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shipwrecked and left on an island is marooned, abandoned like a person thrown off a ship.

clue.text: Shame with a crude blow

parts.note: a bash is a heavy, unsophisticated hit

explanation.surface: Someone is humiliated by a clumsy punch.
explanation.definitionFit: To shame someone is to embarrass or disconcert them, the verb's sense.

clue.text: Source of fruit or vegetable

parts.note: chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: A choice between something from the fruit bowl and a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Apples and pears grow in an orchard of trees, which supplies them.

clue.text: Force through support for the Church

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting an arch or bridge
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Pushing ahead with backing for the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to drive a point into and through something, puncturing it.

clue.text: A case in position

parts.note: a stance is a position, of the body or of opinion

explanation.surface: A legal matter is in a strong position.
explanation.definitionFit: An example or occurrence is a case, as in 'a case in point'.

clue.text: Undue patronage wrongly gets me in post

indicators.note: letters placed wrongly are out of order, so these are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that unfair favouritism has got them a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges ME, IN and POST; 'gets' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring relatives with jobs and positions is improper patronage, unfair use of influence.

clue.text: Animal remains at head of the retreat

indicators.note: one piece is placed at the head, in front, of the other

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Bits of an animal are left at the front of the hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal remains' reads as a carcass; split it instead, with 'at head of' telling us the remains come first. An ashram is a Hindu religious retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermitage or religious community in India is a place of retreat from the world.

clue.text: See hot air wrongly dispelled by rake

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: letters wrongly dispelled are scattered and come back in a new order

explanation.surface: Empty talk is brushed aside by a garden tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly dispelled' rearranges HOT AIR into THARIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a womanising man about town, just like the seducer in an old play whose name became a byword.

clue.text: Change in deep at this time shows barely perceptible rise

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the following letters

explanation.surface: Something in the deep ocean changes, and the sea rises only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges IN DEEP AT; 'this time shows' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest tides of the month, with the least rise and fall, occur near the moon's quarters.

clue.text: Stuffing things in my red taxi

indicators.note: letters stuffed in together are jumbled, so the phrase after it is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone crams their belongings into their red cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a loose signal: the letters of MY RED TAXI are packed in and jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: The craft of preparing and mounting animal skins is a matter of stuffing dead creatures.

clue.text: Net being cast, fish get caught up in it

indicators.note: a net being cast is thrown out, so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod

explanation.surface: As a fishing net is thrown, the fish are trapped in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cast' rearranges NET into ENT; 'in it' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To become tangled is to be caught up in a snarl, the intransitive sense of the verb.

clue.text: Bad drainage? It's the making of this plant!

indicators.note: bad here shows the letters following are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: Poorly drained soil turns out to be just what a certain shrub needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges DRAINAGE; 'It's the making of' links, saying the anagram makes the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers is a plant.

clue.text: At first it turns colour unlike the nudist

indicators.note: first places the word at at the front of the answer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turns means the word it is read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: To begin with, something changes shade, which a naturist would never do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' looks like 'initially', but 'first' is the placing signal and 'At' is a piece; 'turns' reverses the word it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist wears nothing, whereas someone clothed is dressed.

clue.text: Provides flavour I notice going in and out

indicators.note: going in means one piece is placed inside the word and

parts.note: I see means I notice

explanation.surface: Something gives taste; you notice it coming and going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going in' puts I SEE inside AND; 'Provides' and 'out' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of the anise plant, with its liquorice taste, is used to flavour sweets and drinks.

clue.text: Small numbers I'm ill-treating? Enormous number!

indicators.note: ill-treating means handling roughly, so these letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: No. is the short form of number, so numbers made small is Nos

explanation.surface: A patient says the small doses are making them ill, then the bill is huge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treating' rearranges NOS with I'M ILL; 'ill' does double service in the surface's 'ill-treating' but supplies letters only.
explanation.definitionFit: Countless or a vast quantity, as in 'millions of people'.

clue.text: Outcome of a trial-the rope

indicators.note: the outcome of the letters is what they turn into when reworked

explanation.surface: The verdict of a court case is the hangman's noose.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's lasso is a long rope with a noose.

clue.text: Hard beds

parts.note: uncomfortable sleeping places, read instead as geological beds: layers of rock laid down one on another

explanation.definitionFit: Geologists call layers of rock beds, and rock is hard.

clue.text: Registering astonishment at the silver copy

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished at the silver replica.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-mouthed with wonder, as someone surprised stands gaping.

clue.text: A capital letter sounds to be an absolute gift of a clue

indicators.note: sounds tells us the phrase is said aloud to give the entry

parts.note: a big S, a large ess

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that this clue is a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' asks us to say LARGE ESS aloud. The 'absolute gift of a clue' is the setter's joke: the answer itself means generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous giving, especially of money, a liberal present.

clue.text: Angular figure that needs altering

indicators.note: the figure needs the word altering, which is itself a call to rearrange its letters

explanation.surface: A drawing with angles needs correcting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altering' is the fodder and also tells us what to do with it; 'needs' joins the definition to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-sided shape has three angles, a basic angular figure.

clue.text: Band member with permit

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A musician in a group has a licence.
explanation.definitionFit: A band worn round the upper arm, an armband.

clue.text: Endless trouble when I start doing nothing at all

indicators.note: start puts the letter at the beginning of the answer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so its letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: There is no end of bother once you begin to laze about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges ENDLESS; 'start' puts I in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Being idle is being inactive, spending time without any activity.
